question: Recommended number of antenatal visits for a normal pregnancy (WHO/India) is at least:
explanation:
• WHO recommends at least 8 ANC contacts. India's guidelines emphasize quality ANC.
• First visit in first trimester.

question: Stage of labour when cervix is fully dilated:
explanation:
• Second stage: full dilation (10 cm) to delivery of baby.
• First = onset to full dilation; Third = delivery of placenta.

question: Primary cause of postpartum haemorrhage (PPH) is:
explanation:
• Uterine atony (failure of uterus to contract) is the commonest cause of PPH.
• 4 T's: Tone, Trauma, Tissue, Thrombin.

question: Preeclampsia is characterized by:
options: B. Hypertension and proteinuria after 20 weeks
explanation:
• Preeclampsia: BP ≥140/90 and proteinuria after 20 weeks in a previously normotensive woman.
• Can progress to eclampsia (seizures).

question: Bishop score assesses:
explanation:
• Bishop score: cervical dilatation, effacement, consistency, position, fetal station.
• Score ≥8 suggests cervix favorable for induction.

question: Normal blood loss in vaginal delivery is approximately:
explanation:
• Normal vaginal delivery blood loss is about 200-500 ml.
• PPH is typically defined as >500 ml (vaginal) or >1000 ml (C-section).

question: Oxytocin is released from:
explanation:
• Oxytocin is produced in hypothalamus and stored/released from posterior pituitary.
• Stimulates uterine contractions and milk ejection.

question: Placenta praevia is when placenta:
options: B. Implants in lower segment covering/adjacent to internal os
explanation:
• Placenta praevia: placenta in lower uterine segment over or near internal os.
• Presents with painless bleeding; often requires C-section.

question: Apgar score does NOT include:
explanation:
• Apgar: Heart rate, Respiratory effort, Muscle tone, Reflex irritability, Color (Appearance).
• Not blood pressure.

question: Ectopic pregnancy most commonly occurs in:
explanation:
• Most ectopic pregnancies are in the fallopian tube (tubal).
• Rupture can cause life-threatening hemorrhage.

question: First stage of labour ends when:
options: B. Cervix is fully dilated (10 cm)
explanation:
• First stage: onset of labour to full dilatation. Second: full dilatation to birth. Third: birth to placenta.
• Duration varies in primigravida vs multigravida.

question: Magnesium sulfate in eclampsia is given to:
explanation:
• MgSO4 is anticonvulsant for preeclampsia/eclampsia. Monitor reflexes, respiration, urine output.
• Calcium gluconate is antidote for toxicity.

question: Lochia rubra is:
options: B. Red/bloody discharge in first few days postpartum
explanation:
• Lochia rubra: red, first 3-4 days. Lochia serosa: pinkish. Lochia alba: whitish, up to 6 weeks.
• Foul smell suggests infection.

question: Fetal heart rate normal range (bpm) is:
explanation:
• Normal FHR 110-160 bpm. Tachycardia >160; bradycardia <110.
• Continuous monitoring in labour for high-risk.

question: Indication for LSCS (Caesarean) includes:
options: B. CPD, fetal distress, placenta praevia, previous LSCS (depending on case)
explanation:
• LSCS: CPD, fetal distress, placenta praevia, malpresentation, failed induction, etc.
• Balance benefits and risks.

question: Fundal height at 20 weeks gestation is approximately at:
explanation:
• At 20 weeks fundus at umbilicus. Rule of thumb: cm ≈ weeks (20-34).
• Used for growth assessment.

question: Fourth stage of labour is:
options: B. First 1-2 hours after delivery of placenta
explanation:
• Fourth stage: first 1-2 hours postpartum. Monitor bleeding, fundus, vitals, bladder.
• Risk of PPH highest in this period.

question: Rubella infection in early pregnancy can cause:
options: B. Congenital rubella syndrome (deafness, heart defects, cataract)
explanation:
• Congenital rubella: cataract, heart defects, deafness, intellectual disability.
• Vaccinate before pregnancy; avoid pregnancy after MMR.

question: Partograph is used to:
options: B. Monitor progress of labour (cervical dilatation, descent, contractions)
explanation:
• Partograph: cervical dilatation, descent, contractions. Identifies prolonged labour.
• Action line guides when to intervene.

question: Immediate care of newborn after delivery includes:
options: B. Dry, warm, clear airway, assess breathing, Apgar
explanation:
• Dry and warm; clear airway; stimulate if needed; assess breathing; Apgar at 1 and 5 min.
• Delayed cord clamping per protocol.

question: Abruptio placentae presents with:
options: B. Painful bleeding, tender uterus, may have concealed hemorrhage
explanation:
• Abruption: placenta separates before delivery. Painful bleeding; tender uterus; fetal distress.
• Emergency; can cause DIC.

question: Pregnancy test (urine) detects:
explanation:
• Urine/blood pregnancy test detects hCG (produced by placenta).
• Positive around missed period.

question: Episiotomy is:
options: B. Surgical cut in perineum to enlarge vaginal opening
explanation:
• Episiotomy: perineal cut to facilitate delivery. Not routine; use when indicated.
• Repair with sutures; perineal care post-delivery.

question: Anaemia in pregnancy: Hb below ___ g/dL is significant:
explanation:
• WHO: anemia in pregnancy Hb <11 g/dL. Severe <7.
• Iron and folate supplementation.

question: Membrane sweep is:
options: B. Digital separation of membranes from cervix to encourage labour
explanation:
• Membrane sweep: digital separation of chorion from cervix to promote labour.
• Can reduce need for formal induction.

question: Gestational diabetes is:
options: B. Diabetes first diagnosed in pregnancy
explanation:
• GDM: glucose intolerance first recognized in pregnancy. Screen at 24-28 weeks.
• Diet, exercise; insulin if needed. Increases risk of type 2 later.

question: Uterine involution: uterus returns to non-pregnant size by about:
explanation:
• Involution: uterus shrinks to pre-pregnancy size by ~6 weeks.
• Fundal height decreases daily; subinvolution suggests retention or infection.

question: Cord prolapse: immediate action is:
options: B. Relieve cord pressure (e.g. knee-chest, fill bladder), prepare for urgent delivery
explanation:
• Cord prolapse: cord ahead of presenting part. Relieve pressure (knee-chest, Trendelenburg, or fill bladder).
• Urgent delivery (often C-section).

question: Postpartum blues typically occur:
explanation:
• Baby blues: mild mood changes, tearfulness in first 1-2 weeks. Usually self-limiting.
• Different from postpartum depression (persistent, severe).

question: Tocolytics are used to:
explanation:
• Tocolytics: delay preterm labour (e.g. nifedipine, atosiban). Buy time for steroids.
• Not for term or when delivery indicated.

question: Folic acid in pregnancy is important for:
options: B. Prevention of neural tube defects
explanation:
• Folic acid before and early pregnancy reduces neural tube defects (spina bifida).
• 400-800 mcg daily.

question: Shoulder dystocia: maneuver includes:
options: B. McRoberts (hyperflex legs), suprapubic pressure, other maneuvers
explanation:
• Shoulder dystocia: head delivered, shoulders stuck. McRoberts, suprapubic pressure, Woods screw, etc.
• Call for help; document.

question: Postpartum hemorrhage (PPH) is blood loss:
explanation:
• PPH: >500 ml vaginal or >1000 ml C-section. Can be primary (24 h) or secondary (24 h–12 weeks).
• 4 T's: Tone, Trauma, Tissue, Thrombin.

question: Amniotic fluid volume is assessed by:
explanation:
• AFI (amniotic fluid index) or single deepest pocket on ultrasound.
• Oligohydramnios/hydramnios have implications.

question: Contraindication to breastfeeding includes:
options: B. Maternal HIV in some settings (per guidelines), active TB until treated, certain drugs
explanation:
• HIV: guidelines vary (ART may allow BF in some). Active untreated TB: avoid until treated. Some drugs contraindicated.
• Support when safe.
